title: Sigil and Salt Again
premise: In the salt-hazed city of Verrin, magic was outlawed a generation ago, and Astrid Lockridge has survived by selling charms too small to notice—until the old gods, starved of worship, begin answering prayers again and her hidden sigils start burning with borrowed power. When her brother's soul is revealed as collateral in a bargain their dead mother struck with the court beneath the mountain, Astrid must ally with a disgraced inquisitor and a god who has forgotten its own name to steal it back. Each act of open magic makes her more visible—and less human—as the gods' attention reshapes her. In the end, Astrid wins her brother's freedom by surrendering her own name to the court, becoming something new: neither god nor mortal, but the living sigil through which Verrin's outlawed magic finally returns.
about_author: Xanthe Yarrow is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing folk charms in coastal fishing towns before turning to fiction. They write about small magics, stubborn survivors, and the debts families leave behind.

chapters.title: The Charm Seller's Hour
chapters.summary: Astrid works the dawn markets of Verrin, trading luck-knots and salt wards while dodging inquisitors' patrols. A customer's dying prayer is answered by something old, and one of Astrid's inert sigils flares alive. POV: Astrid. Emotional beat: wary wonder—the first crack in ten years of careful invisibility.

chapters.title: Salt on the Threshold
chapters.summary: Astrid tests her waking sigils in secret and finds they draw power from answered prayers she never made. Her guildmaster, Halvard, warns her that when gods wake, they collect old debts. POV: Astrid. Emotional beat: dread beneath curiosity; the past knocking.

chapters.title: What Mother Buried
chapters.summary: Searching her late mother's effects, Astrid finds a contract sealed in ash: her brother Tam's soul pledged to the court beneath the mountain as payment for the family's survival during the purges. POV: Astrid. Emotional beat: betrayal and grief reframing her whole childhood.

chapters.title: The Inquisitor Who Quit
chapters.summary: Astrid seeks out Sera Duvane, an ex-inquisitor who once burned her own order's records and now drinks in the Low Quarter. Duvane knows the mountain court's laws—and its loopholes. POV: Duvane. Emotional beat: bitter recognition between two women hiding from institutions.

chapters.title: Prayers Answered Wrong
chapters.summary: Across Verrin, desperate prayers are being granted with cruel literalism; a fisherman's wish drowns his rivals. The awakened gods are starving and imprecise. Astrid realizes unchecked, they will gut the city. POV: rotating street vignettes into Astrid. Emotional beat: guilt—her sigils are part of the circuit.

chapters.title: Down the Stair of Teeth
chapters.summary: Guided by Duvane's stolen maps, Astrid descends the smugglers' stair toward the mountain court's outer halls, where bargains are recorded in bone ledgers. She sees Tam's name among the entries. POV: Astrid. Emotional beat: awe curdling into resolve.

chapters.title: The Clerk of Debts
chapters.summary: Astrid negotiates with the Clerk, a faceless functionary who explains the terms: a soul may be redeemed only by an equivalent pledge. It offers her a form to sign. She refuses and flees. POV: Astrid. Emotional beat: terror of bureaucracy that devours; refusal as first defiance.

chapters.title: A God With No Name
chapters.summary: Hiding in the deep galleries, Astrid encounters a wretched, amnesiac god chained beneath the court—a deity erased from all records. It begs her for its name. She recognizes its sigil: it matches her own birthmark. POV: Astrid. Emotional beat: pity and uncanny kinship.

chapters.title: Ten Years Invisible
chapters.summary: Flashback chapter: young Astrid learning charm-craft from her mother, the purges closing in, the night the family made its bargain. POV: alternating mother/Astrid. Emotional beat: understanding how love and desperation forged the debt she now inherits.

chapters.title: The Guild's Last Vote
chapters.summary: Astrid returns and confesses everything to the surviving guild members. Halvard argues for silence; the youngest argue for action. The guild votes, barely, to help her steal the ledger page bearing Tam's contract. POV: ensemble, anchored on Astrid. Emotional beat: fragile solidarity against extinction.

chapters.title: Smoke Over the Low Quarter
chapters.summary: The court's enforcers surface to punish the escaped debtor; a raid burns half the Low Quarter. Duvane's old order offers her reinstatement if she delivers Astrid. POV: Duvane. Emotional beat: temptation of belonging versus loyalty to a friend.

chapters.title: Learning to Burn
chapters.summary: Training montage of a different kind: Astrid practices wielding the nameless god's power through her sigils, each spell costing her memories of her mother. POV: Astrid. Emotional beat: the price of survival made literal—power eating identity.

chapters.title: The Ledger Heist
chapters.summary: The guild executes a coordinated theft inside the bone archive: distractions, forged prayers, Duvane's credentials. They secure the page—but the Clerk anticipated them, and the true contract is elsewhere. POV: multiple, converging on Astrid. Emotional beat: triumph flipping to trap.

chapters.title: Betrayal in Bone
chapters.summary: Duvane's former colleagues arrive; exposed, Duvane must choose publicly. She burns her reinstatement oath and joins Astrid, taking an inquisitor's brand across her own hands. POV: Duvane. Emotional beat: redemption purchased with permanent cost.

chapters.title: Tam, Awake
chapters.summary: Astrid reaches Tam's cell within the court. He is lucid but fading, his memories traded away in installments he doesn't remember selling. He asks her not to save him at the city's expense. POV: Tam. Emotional beat: heartbreak—he'd rather be lost than be her reason to become a monster.

chapters.title: The Court Beneath the Mountain
chapters.summary: Dragged before the court's seated powers, Astrid learns the truth: the gods were caged deliberately after the purges, and her mother's bargain helped build the cage. The court offers her Tam's freedom in exchange for becoming its new Clerk. POV: Astrid. Emotional beat: the seduction of a just-seeming tyranny.

chapters.title: Justice Outside the Law
chapters.summary: Refusing both the court's law and the guild's caution, Astrid frees the nameless god using her own name as the key—unbinding every record in the archive. Chaos erupts; debts dissolve; the mountain begins to crack. POV: Astrid. Emotional beat: liberation as catastrophe; no clean hands.

chapters.title: When the Gods Remember
chapters.summary: Freed gods flood Verrin, answering every prayer at once. Astrid, half-dissolved into pure sigil, walks the burning streets teaching them restraint—bargaining prayer by prayer. POV: shifting god-perspectives and Astrid. Emotional beat: exhaustion transfigured into strange grace.

chapters.title: The Price Named Twice
chapters.summary: At the collapsing heart of the court, Astrid confronts the Clerk one last time. To seal the new covenant—magic lawful, souls sovereign—she must give up her name permanently. Tam, restored, tries to take her place. POV: alternating siblings. Emotional beat: love arguing with sacrifice.

chapters.title: Sigil and Salt
chapters.summary: Astrid speaks her name into the foundation stone; the covenant takes hold. The mountain quiets, the gods settle into fair bargains, and Tam walks free carrying her memory of herself. POV: Tam watching Astrid become light and line. Emotional beat: grief braided with triumph.

chapters.title: The Woman Made of Marks
chapters.summary: A year later, Verrin thrives with licensed small magics. A figure of glowing sigils tends the shrine where the nameless god now keeps its recovered name. Tam leaves offerings; sometimes the figure pauses, almost remembering. POV: Tam. Emotional beat: bittersweet continuity—love persisting past identity.

chapters.title: Again
chapters.summary: On the anniversary, a child prays at the shrine and the sigil-woman answers gently, fairly—for the first time choosing whom to help. In that choice, a fragment of Astrid re-coalesces around the act itself. POV: Astrid. Emotional beat: hope earned, not given—an ending that is also a beginning.
